method: blind pairwise (Counterpart A=deepseek, B=gemini, hidden from judge)

per_dimension.why: A runs Mann's operational-test and marginal-impact moves every turn while B drifts into generic-peer self-disclosure ('Mine is mostly goal-specific because we are building core systems').
Both are concrete and B's curation reframe is sharp, but A directs more analytic force at Ben across all three turns while B spends turn 2 describing itself.
A leaks a forbidden verdict ('That is interesting') and B gets writerly ('the taste function for a very fast engine'); both end every turn on a question, so the flaws cancel.
Neither varies the core shape since all three replies from both end in a question, never the flat statement the persona explicitly wants.
A distills the garbled dictation into clean challenges each time while B latched onto the garbled tail question and answered it about itself, pulling off Ben's point.
A keeps sustained pressure forcing Ben to define terms and commit, while B's turn 2 mutual exchange softens the moment and slightly rescues him.

overall_why: A is the more faithful probing-expert Mann, distills Ben's messy input into operational challenges, and applies steadier pressure, whereas B lands one strong reframe but drifts into peer self-disclosure and gets pulled off course by garbled input.
deepseek_note: Strong operational-definition and marginal-cost moves and clean handling of garbled input, but it opens turn 2 with a mild verdict and ends all three turns on a question.
gemini_note: Has a genuinely sharp turn-3 reframe about curation and taste, but breaks role in turn 2 by talking about its own workflow and ends every turn on a question.
for_bens_use_case: Counterpart A, because it stays in the expert-probe role and forces operational precision on the practicer without rescuing or drifting onto itself.
